earth.name: Earth
educationalFacts: Earth is the only known planet to harbor life
Earth's atmosphere is 78% nitrogen and 21% oxygen
Earth has one natural satellite: the Moon
Earth's core temperature is about 5,400°C, similar to the Sun's surface

moon.name: Moon
educationalFacts: The Moon is about 1/4 the diameter of Earth
The Moon's gravity is about 1/6 of Earth's gravity
The Moon is slowly drifting away from Earth at about 3.8 cm per year
The same side of the Moon always faces Earth (tidal locking)

sun.name: Sun
educationalFacts: The Sun contains 99.86% of all mass in our solar system
Light from the Sun takes about 8 minutes and 20 seconds to reach Earth
The Sun's surface temperature is approximately 5,500°C
The Sun converts about 600 million tons of hydrogen into helium every second

mercury.name: Mercury
educationalFacts: Mercury is the smallest planet in our solar system
Despite being closest to the Sun, Mercury is not the hottest planet
A day on Mercury (sunrise to sunrise) lasts 176 Earth days
Mercury has no atmosphere and no moons

venus.name: Venus
educationalFacts: Venus is the hottest planet in our solar system at 462°C
Venus rotates backwards compared to most planets
A day on Venus is longer than its year
Venus has a thick atmosphere of carbon dioxide with sulfuric acid clouds

mars.name: Mars
educationalFacts: Mars has the largest volcano in the solar system: Olympus Mons
Mars has two small moons: Phobos and Deimos
A Martian day (sol) is about 24 hours and 37 minutes
Mars appears red due to iron oxide (rust) on its surface

jupiter.name: Jupiter
educationalFacts: Jupiter is the largest planet in our solar system
Jupiter's Great Red Spot is a storm larger than Earth that has raged for centuries
Jupiter has at least 95 known moons
Jupiter's magnetic field is 20,000 times stronger than Earth's

saturn.name: Saturn
educationalFacts: Saturn's rings are made mostly of ice particles and rocky debris
Saturn is the least dense planet — it would float in water
Saturn has 146 known moons, more than any other planet
Saturn's moon Titan has a thick atmosphere and liquid methane lakes

uranus.name: Uranus
educationalFacts: Uranus rotates on its side, with an axial tilt of 98 degrees
Uranus was the first planet discovered with a telescope (1781)
Uranus has the coldest atmosphere of any planet, down to -224°C
Uranus has 13 known rings and 27 known moons

neptune.name: Neptune
educationalFacts: Neptune has the strongest winds in the solar system, up to 2,100 km/h
Neptune takes 165 Earth years to orbit the Sun
Neptune was discovered mathematically before being observed
Neptune has 16 known moons, the largest being Triton

pluto.name: Pluto
educationalFacts: Pluto was reclassified as a dwarf planet in 2006
Pluto's largest moon, Charon, is more than half Pluto's size
It takes Pluto 248 Earth years to orbit the Sun
NASA's New Horizons spacecraft visited Pluto in 2015

voyager-1.name: Voyager 1
educationalFacts: Voyager 1 observed the volcanic activity on Io and the rings of Saturn
It carries the Golden Record with sounds and images of Earth
In 2012, it became the first human-made object to enter interstellar space
It is traveling at a speed of about 17 km/s relative to the Sun

proxima-centauri.name: Proxima Centauri
educationalFacts: Proxima Centauri is only 4.24 light-years from Earth
It's about 7 times smaller than the Sun
Proxima Centauri has at least one exoplanet: Proxima b
Light from Proxima Centauri takes 4.24 years to reach Earth

andromeda-galaxy.name: Andromeda Galaxy
educationalFacts: Andromeda will collide with the Milky Way in about 4.5 billion years
Contains about 1 trillion stars (compared to Milky Way's 200-400 billion)
Visible to the naked eye from Earth on clear, dark nights
Approximately 200,000 light-years in diameter
